What the SRS says: The system shall let a user sign up and sign in using only an email address and a 6-digit OTP sent to that address.
The system shall reject any email address not ending in @thapar.edu (case-insensitive) both in the app and in the database, so that no account is created and no OTP is sent.
On creation of an authentication account, the system shall automatically create a matching profile row in users with role student and id_verified = pending.
The system shall require the student to enter a roll number consisting of 9–10 digits, and shall store it on the profile.
The system shall let the student upload a photograph of their student ID card (JPEG, PNG, HEIC or WebP; max 8 MB), store it privately, and set id_verified to pending.
The system shall allow a student whose ID card was rejected to upload a new photograph.
The system shall display the user's profile, including email, roll number, verification status and role.
The system shall let the user sign out, ending the session on the device.
The system shall keep the user signed in across app restarts until they sign out or the session expires.
Where a registrar-provided student list is available, the system should cross-check the entered roll number against it.
Note: No registrar student list is available yet; ID cards are checked by an admin instead (FR-ADM-3/4).

What the SRS says: The system shall display a feed of listings whose status is live, newest first, to both guests and signed-in users.
The system shall let users filter the feed by type (Sell, Lend, Exchange) and by category (Textbooks, Electronics, Lab & Drafter, Cycle & Commute, Sports Gear, Stationery).
The system shall let users search listings by keyword, case-insensitively, over title and description.
The system shall show a listing detail screen with photographs, title, description, category, condition, price or rent terms or wanted items, and meeting location.
For a request without a valid session, the backend shall replace the meeting location with null and mark it hidden; the app shall prompt the guest to sign in to see it.
The system shall prompt a guest to sign in when they attempt any action other than browsing (chat, list, offer).
The system shall return the feed in pages of 20 listings by default and never more than 50 per request.
The system should allow sorting listings by proximity of the meeting point to the viewer's hostel.

The system shall allow a verified student to create a listing with: type (sell / lend / exchange), title (3–120 characters), optional description (up to 2000 characters), category, condition (Like New / Good / Fair) and meeting location.

The system shall require a price for a Sell listing, a rent amount (with unit day or week) for a Lend listing, and at least one wanted-item tag (max 10) for an Exchange listing, and shall reject a listing missing its type-specific field.
The system shall let the user attach up to 6 photographs (images only, max 8 MB each) to a listing, stored in public storage under the owner's folder.
The system shall offer the meeting location as a choice from the campus list (18 hostels and campus spots such as Library, Main Gate and Sports Complex), and the backend shall refuse any other value.
The system shall save every new listing with status pending_review and never publish it directly.
The system shall show a user all of their own listings at every status (pending review, live, reserved, completed, removed).
The system shall allow only the owner of a listing to delete it; any other user shall receive a "forbidden" response.
The system should allow the owner to edit a listing; an edited live listing shall return to moderation.
The system shall mark a listing reserved once a buyer is selected and completed once the transaction closes.
When a listing is created, the system shall insert a corresponding entry into the moderation queue with status pending; if this fails, the listing shall be rolled back.
The system shall show administrators the queue of pending listings with full listing details.
An administrator shall be able to approve a listing, which sets the listing to live and records the reviewer and time.
An administrator shall be able to reject a listing with a reason, which sets the listing to removed.
The system shall record submission and decision timestamps so that TLC can be measured.
The system should notify the owner when their listing is approved or rejected, including the reason.
The system may obtain a confidence score from an off-the-shelf moderation API to help prioritise the queue; it shall never auto-reject on that score.
Note: No AI moderation service is connected; every listing gets human review. Tested: no score is set and nothing is auto-rejected.

What the SRS says: Any signed-in student shall be able to report a live listing, or another student they have chatted with, choosing a reason (scam, fake, prohibited item, wrong details, offensive, other) and adding optional details. A student may have only one open report per listing or person, and cannot report their own listing or themselves.

Administrators shall see open reports with what was reported, by whom and how many open reports it has, and shall dismiss each one or act on it with a note. Acting on a listing report, or taking a listing down directly, shall remove the listing from the feed for good, call off and refund any deal on it that has not reached the handoff, and close every open report on that listing.

The system shall notify administrators of each new report, tell the owner why their listing was taken down (also shown on the listing and under My listings), tell both parties when a deal is called off by a takedown, and tell each reporter the outcome.

The system shall let a verified student start a chat on another student's live listing; there shall be at most one thread per buyer per listing, and starting it again shall return the existing thread. Students whose ID is not verified, and guests, cannot start a chat.
The system shall prevent a user from starting a chat on their own listing.
The system shall let participants send text messages and view the thread's history in time order (up to the latest 200 messages).
The system shall list a user's chat threads, each with its listing and last message.
The system shall return "forbidden" to any user who is not a participant of a thread for every message or offer operation.
Either participant shall be able to propose a price offer; only the other participant shall be able to accept or reject it.
Accepting an offer shall automatically reject all other pending offers in that thread, and no further offers shall be allowed in that thread.
The app shall show messages and offers in one combined timeline ordered by time.
The seller shall be able to choose one buyer among several concurrent negotiations and finalise the deal, creating a transaction.
Messages should be delivered in real time (Supabase Realtime) rather than by polling.
Note: Delivered through Supabase Realtime instead of a separate WebSocket server.

What the SRS says: A deal shall be confirmed by both parties: one participant proposes the terms and only the other can accept them; the owner finalises the accepted terms, at exactly that price; the payer confirms by paying into escrow; and the receiver confirms the handoff by scanning the QR code.
When a deal is finalised, the system shall create a transaction recording listing, type, buyer, seller, agreed price and meeting location, with status pending_payment.
The system shall collect the buyer's payment through the payment gateway and hold it in escrow (status escrow_held). In the pilot the gateway is simulated: the hold is recorded but no money moves.
Note: Payment gateway not connected yet: "pay" records the money as held in escrow. All escrow rules are tested.

What the SRS says: For Lend transactions, the system shall record start date, end date, deposit amount and rent per day.
The system shall release escrow to the seller only after a successful handoff (and, for Lend, a completed return).
The system shall refund the buyer if the transaction is cancelled before handoff or a dispute is decided in the buyer's favour.
The system shall show both parties the current transaction status.

Either party shall be able to cancel a deal before the handoff (pending payment, escrow held or QR issued). Any money held is refunded, every QR code for the deal stops working, and the listing returns to live. A deal cannot be cancelled once the item has changed hands, while it is disputed, or by anyone else.

For an Exchange, escrow shall hold the agreed top-up, if any. The person asking to swap names and photographs their item; either side may add a top-up and must say who pays it; only that side can pay it; on a completed handoff it goes to the other side, and a cancelled swap returns it to the payer. A straight swap holds Rs. 0 and goes straight to the meetup.
After payment is held, the system shall issue a random, single-use QR code for the transaction that expires after 10 minutes (status qr_issued).
At the meeting, the counter-party shall scan the QR code in the app; the system shall accept it only if it is valid, unexpired, unused and belongs to that transaction.
The system shall require condition photographs to be captured at handoff and store them against the transaction.
On a valid scan, the system shall mark the token used, and for Sell/Exchange shall complete the transaction and release escrow.
Either party shall be able to flag a discrepancy at handoff instead of confirming, which moves the transaction to disputed.

If a QR code expires, the giver shall be able to show a new one, which replaces the old. If a party does not turn up, either party may cancel before the handoff (FR-PAY-7) or report it as a problem, which freezes the money for an administrator (FR-HND-5).
For a Lend transaction, the system shall keep it open after handoff until the item is returned.
The system shall require return-stage condition photographs and a QR-verified return.
The system should remind the borrower before the due date and flag overdue items.
On a confirmed return with no reported issue, the system shall settle rent and refund the deposit.
A party to a transaction shall be able to raise one dispute per transaction with a reason.
The system shall freeze escrow while a dispute is open.
Administrators shall see open disputes with handoff and return condition photographs side by side.
An administrator shall be able to request more evidence, then resolve the dispute with a written resolution, releasing or refunding escrow.
An administrator may apply a penalty amount to the party at fault, per pre-defined penalty tiers.
The system shall notify both parties of each change in dispute status.
The system shall store in-app notifications per user with a type, payload and read/unread flag.
The system shall notify users of listing decisions, new messages and offers, transaction updates and dispute updates.
The system should let a student subscribe to categories and alert them when a matching listing goes live (and match Exchange want-tags).
The system shall show an admin-only Review tab to users with role = admin.
The backend shall re-check the caller's admin role from the database on every /admin request, returning 403 to non-admins, regardless of what the app displays.
The system shall show admins pending ID cards, each via a signed URL valid for 10 minutes.
An admin shall be able to mark an ID card verified or rejected.

The system should show platform analytics: TLC (median, 90th percentile and share decided within 24 hours), listing volume by type, transaction completion rate, the share of transactions that are lend/borrow, the on-time return rate, and the dispute rate for lend deals and for all deals.
A separate web dashboard may be provided for administrators. The admin screens run in a web browser and serve as this dashboard.
Note: The admin Review tab also runs in a web browser (Expo web), which serves as the web dashboard.
